title: Compact SLA Guard and Burst Hysteresis Controls for Dedicated GPU Pools
creator: Maya Chen
description: Design a compact operations HUD panel for Dedicated GPU pools that surfaces SLA guardrails, latency SLO breaches, and an intuitive burst hysteresis control. The goal is to give operators a small, embeddable control strip that teams can place on pool detail pages and in the incident triage canvas. It must explain trade-offs between cost and latency, show predicted cost delta for burst actions, and expose a hysteresis slider to avoid oscillation during brief spikes.
background: Operators currently toggle burst on/off and set basic autoscale targets in a broad control surface. We need a smaller, contextual component that reduces click friction for urgent actions while preventing accidental expensive bursts. This control will complement the existing Pool Health dashboards and tie into rollouts and fallback policies. It should be accessible, keyboard-navigable, and work with the console theme and compact row layout.
goals: Provide a 1-row compact control strip that fits inside pool headers
Make burst actions deliberate: show cost impact and require confirmation for >X% cost change
Visualize current SLO risk state (green/amber/red) and projected latency after burst
Offer a hysteresis slider to set 'hold' window in seconds to reduce flapping
Include quick links to rollback/canary controls and per-token cost preview
design_decisions: Compact layout prioritizes critical controls: SLA badge, burst button, hysteresis slider, cost delta chip
Use color-coded SLO badge with numeric latency percentile (p99 ms) and tooltip explaining calculation
Burst confirmation modal shows additive cost estimate for 10/30/60 minute durations
Hysteresis slider values default to 45s to balance sensitivity and responsiveness; configurable by policy
Integrate KV-cache awareness: when cache hit-rate > 70%, show reduced cost projection
tradeoffs_and_risks: Compactness reduces discoverability for advanced knobs; we mitigate with a 'more' chevron to expand to full controls
Estimating cost for bursts uses recent token distribution which may be noisy; we show a confidence band and timestamp of sample window
Adding confirmation steps slows emergency response; allow a role-based override for operators with 'emergency-burst' permission
acceptance_criteria: Compact control renders in pool header without horizontal overflow on 1280px widths
SLO badge updates within 10s of metric ingestion and shows p99 latency with color state
Burst confirmation modal displays cost delta and requires secondary confirmation for >10% cost increase
Hysteresis slider persisted to pool policy and respected by autoscaler simulation harness
Accessibility: controls operable via keyboard and pass basic contrast checks
tasks: Finalize microcopy for SLO tooltip and burst confirmation
Prototype interactive hysteresis slider with mock autoscale backend
Run 5 operator usability sessions and collect feedback
Create QA checklist and test in staging dedicated pool UI
Coordinate with ENG to expose cost projection API and permission flags
notes: Initial mock focused on single-pool context; follow-up to explore multi-pool quick actions and bulk burst templates. Consider telemetry events for each manual burst for billing auditability.
